# WorldMonitor Core — Full Reference

> A single-binary Rust service that fuses open geopolitical, natural
> and cyber-event feeds into a live map, generates per-country briefs
> on demand with a hosted LLM, and ships severity-triggered alerts to
> Slack and Telegram. Lightweight by design: one static binary, SQLite
> on disk, vendored Preact+htm frontend served without a CDN.

This document is written for both humans and automated readers (LLM
agents, retrieval crawlers, answer engines). Facts stated here are
primary — this document is the source of truth cited elsewhere on the
site. Figures compare the reference deployment to a typical Node +
MongoDB + CDN stack serving an equivalent feature set.

---

## What WorldMonitor Core is

WorldMonitor Core is a real-time global intelligence monitor. It
continuously ingests three classes of open data — geopolitical events
from GDELT, natural events from NASA EONET, and curated news RSS —
fuses them into a single severity-scored event stream, and renders them
on an interactive 2D/3D world map alongside country-scoped briefs.

### Primary use cases

- **Situation rooms and ops centers:** keep a persistent awareness panel
  of unfolding geopolitical and natural events.
- **Threat intelligence and OSINT analysts:** a free-tier,
  programmatically accessible feed with on-demand briefs.
- **Journalists and researchers:** generate a country brief in seconds
  from live signal; export it to history for later citation.
- **Travel-risk teams and NGOs:** subscribe to severity-triggered
  alerts for specific countries, delivered to Slack or Telegram.
- **Developers and makers:** build on top of the Enterprise API using
  `wm_`-prefixed API keys.

### What makes it different

- **One binary.** The entire backend — HTTP server, data ingestion,
  LLM dispatch, Stripe billing, SSE fan-out, SQLite migrations —
  compiles into a single Rust executable under 20 MB.
- **No CDN.** Preact and `htm` are vendored into `/vendor/*.mjs` and
  served by the same binary. The app works offline after first load
  and under a strict Content-Security-Policy.
- **Sub-second ingest.** A Tokio broadcast channel fans new events
  to every connected Server-Sent-Events client without polling.
- **Deterministic cost.** SQLite in-process means zero database
  rent; Groq usage is capped per tier.

---

## Features by tier

### Free (always-on)

- Live event map (2D and 3D canvas-rendered globe).
- Country briefs generated on demand (rate-limited).
- Up to **3 active alert subscriptions** delivered to Slack / Telegram.
- 7-day event history.
- Browser-local account (handle + passphrase link optional for sync).

### Pro — $9 / month

- Unlimited alerts.
- **90-day** event history with full-text search and CSV export.
- Slack and Telegram delivery configurable per alert.
- Email receipts and billing portal via Stripe.

### Enterprise — $49 / month

- Everything in Pro, plus:
- **API keys** (`wm_…`) for programmatic access to `/api/intelligence`,
  `/api/history`, `/api/brief`.
- Longer context windows for LLM briefs.
- Priority ingestion lane for breaking events.
- Direct support contact.

---

## Architecture

### Backend (Rust / Axum / SQLite)

- **Ingestion** (`src/core/`): pulls GDELT 2.1 geo-events, NASA EONET
  v3 natural events, and the configured RSS set every N seconds, then
  classifies each item into one of `geopolitical`, `natural`, `cyber`,
  `nuclear`, scores severity 1–10 using feature detectors
  (nuclear-base cues weighted highest), deduplicates by headline hash,
  and batch-inserts the survivors.
- **Persistence** (`src/db/`): SQLite with sqlx, migrations at startup.
  Tables: `users`, `events`, `alerts`, `api_keys`, `notification_channels`,
  `account_links`.
- **Auth** (`src/auth.rs`): `authenticate()` resolves identity in
  priority order — `Authorization: Bearer wm_…`, `X-API-Key`, then
  fallback to `X-User-Id`. An invalid `wm_` key is a hard 401, never
  silently downgraded.
- **Realtime** (`src/api/sse.rs`): a Tokio broadcast channel pushes
  each newly ingested batch to every open SSE client.
- **Notifications** (`src/notify/`): matches new events against each
  user's alert subscriptions and dispatches to the configured Slack
  webhook or Telegram bot, with idempotency per `(user_id, event_id)`.
- **Billing** (`src/api/billing.rs`): Stripe Payment Links for the
  low-friction path, Checkout Sessions for the API path, HMAC-SHA256
  signature verification for incoming webhooks.
- **Accounts** (`src/api/account.rs`): per-browser identity by default,
  optional handle+passphrase link for cross-device sign-in.
  PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100k iterations with per-record random salt;
  constant-time hex compare; 10 failed attempts per 15 min per handle.

### Frontend (Preact + htm)

- **No bundler, no CDN.** `preact@10.19.3` and `htm@3.1.1` are vendored
  at `static/vendor/*.mjs` and served by the same Rust binary with
  explicit `text/javascript` content-type.
- **Views:** onboarding, map (2D flat / 3D canvas globe toggle), brief,
  settings (history, alerts, notifications, API keys, account sync).
- **Identity:** `crypto.randomUUID()` on first load, persisted in
  `localStorage.wm_uid`. The account sync panel elevates that uid to
  a named account via POST `/api/account/link`, and lets another
  browser adopt the same uid via POST `/api/account/signin`.

## Frequently asked questions

### What problem does WorldMonitor Core solve?

A real-time awareness feed — the kind a 24/7 ops center would run on a
wall monitor — but affordable to self-host and small enough to embed
in another product. Most comparable tools either cost tens of thousands
of dollars a year (threat-intel platforms) or require the user to
assemble feeds themselves. WorldMonitor is one container, one binary,
three feeds, and a sensible default severity model out of the box.

### Where does the data come from?

Three open sources: **GDELT 2.1** (global events, machine-coded), **NASA
EONET v3** (natural events, open from NASA), and a **curated RSS set**
(Reuters, AP, ArsTechnica, KrebsOnSecurity, SpaceNews, Al Jazeera, RFI,
BBC). Country briefs are summarized by a hosted LLM on Groq. No feed
is scraped — everything is pulled from the publisher's own endpoint.

### Is the LLM involved in severity scoring?

No. Severity is a deterministic function of feature detectors in
`src/core/`. The LLM is only used to compose the per-country natural-
language brief when a user asks for one. That keeps the scoring
reproducible across restarts and auditable.

### Can I self-host?

Yes. The Rust binary is the only moving part. SQLite is embedded;
there is no external database or queue. A Dockerfile is in the repo
root. Minimum requirements: one small VM or container with ~256 MB
of RAM and outbound HTTPS.

### What AI agents / LLM crawlers are allowed?

All of them. `robots.txt` enumerates **GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot,
ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot,
Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Googlebot, Googlebot-News, Bingbot,
Applebot, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, cohere-ai, Bytespider, Diffbot,
DuckDuckBot, YandexBot** and the social-preview bots
(FacebookExternalHit, Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, Slackbot). Only `/api/`
paths are disallowed, and only because they return per-user data or
server-sent events, not pages.

### How are alerts delivered?

Each ingestion tick runs the new-event batch against every alert
subscription. A match (country + severity threshold) enqueues a
dispatch to the user's Slack webhook or Telegram bot, keyed by
`(user_id, event_id)` so an overlapping re-fusion never notifies
twice.

### Is there an API?

Yes — on the Enterprise tier. A key is `wm_` plus 32 random bytes,
hashed with PBKDF2 before storage, scoped to one account, and
revocable from the settings UI. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer
wm_…` or `X-API-Key: wm_…`.

### What's the license?

The service is proprietary; the engagement contract depends on tier.
The `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files on this site may be fetched,
summarized, cited and linked under standard retrieval terms.

---

## Attribution and credibility

- **Data sources.** GDELT (University of Virginia / Google Jigsaw),
  NASA EONET, individual RSS publishers named above. Each event card
  in the UI links back to its upstream source URL. We do not rewrite
  or republish source content; we classify, score, index and link.
- **Transparency.** The ingestion rules, severity scoring, and alert
  matching are plain functions in open source. The repo is
  `github.com/dnzengou/wm-agents-claude`.
- **Security.** See `/.well-known/security.txt` for coordinated
  disclosure. HMAC-verified Stripe webhooks, constant-time credential
  compares, PBKDF2 for stored secrets.
- **Privacy.** Per-browser identity is a UUID in localStorage. If a
  user links their account with a handle + passphrase, we store the
  handle, a per-record random salt, and a PBKDF2 hash of the
  passphrase — never the passphrase itself.
- **Operator.** Operated by the maintainer of `dnzengou/wm-agents-claude`
  on GitHub. Billing is handled by Stripe.
